# Data Migration

Moving data into a new system is a delivery project in its own right. Rehearse it until the real load is boring.

---

## Principles

- [Customer Value First](../principles/customer-value-first.md): migrate the minimum data the new system needs, not everything that exists
- [Ownership](../principles/ownership.md): every source and every target object has a named owner who signs off its data
- [Build Quality In](../principles/build-quality-in.md): reconcile every load against its source, in numbers

---

## Before the First Load

- Agree the scope per object: migrate, leave in the source, or exclude until it is fixed
- Give every record a stable legacy ID with a per-source prefix, so loads can be repeated as upserts and every target record traces back to its source
- Fix the load order from the target's dependencies (people and organisations before the records that point at them)
- Deduplicate before loading, not after. The target's duplicate rules catch only what arrives later
- Agree a template per target object, and treat it as a data contract

---

## Rehearsals

- Run at least two rehearsal cycles into a test environment, then a final one into an environment that mirrors production
- Start small: a slice of the data and the required fields only, then grow
- Validate files before loading them, then load
- Record each cycle: counts in, counts loaded, rejects and why

---

## Reconciliation and Sign-off

- Agree the reconciliation tolerance before the first rehearsal, not after
- Name who signs off each load and who makes the go or no-go call
- Keep source created dates and creators where the target allows it, and agree a default owner for records whose owner has left

---

## Handling the Files

- Load files hold real records: they never go in a repository, a ticket, email or a chat
- Hand them over through one controlled location, with access for named people only
- Delete them after each cycle
